key_insight: In WTaCrV, collision cascades split into subcascades more often than in pure W, spreading energy over a larger volume and reducing severe defect formation.
engineering_relevance: This suggests equimolar refractory alloys can offer improved radiation tolerance for fusion and other high-dose environments compared with pure tungsten.
method: Molecular dynamics simulations across 0.1–100 keV PKA energies
Machine-learning tabGAP interatomic potential with short-range ZBL repulsion
Compared cascade morphology, atomic relocations, and surviving defects in pure W vs WTaCrV
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that WTaCrV shows more frequent cascade splitting, fewer dislocations, and no voids, while pure W forms smaller voids.
watch_item: The conclusions are based on atomistic simulations and may depend on the interatomic potential and the specific composition/irradiation conditions studied.
paper_title: Collision Cascade Morphology and Defect Nucleation in Pure Tungsten and an Equimolar Refractory W-Ta-Cr-V Alloy
